tasks.prompt: Summarise the rules a Linguaroo squad must follow when it creates a feature flag and rolls it out.

rubric.text: Every flag needs a named owner and an expiry date: release flags at most 90 days, experiment flags at most 45 days, and kill switches have no expiry.
Each app holds at most 200 active flags, and names are lower case with underscores and start with the squad prefix.
A flag must never change what a learner pays or gate a paid feature.
A squad may roll out to up to 10% on its own; going past 10% needs a second person from the squad to approve in Pennant.
Going to 100% on a weekend is not allowed, except for kill switches.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-c

tasks.prompt: Explain how the Linguaroo iOS and Android apps get and use flag values, including when a learner is offline for a long time.

rubric.text: Flags are evaluated on the device by the Pennant SDK, not resolved on the server.
The apps download the ruleset at launch and every 30 minutes while the app is open.
A cached ruleset is used for up to 7 days without a refresh; after that the apps fall back to the defaults compiled into the build.
A flag check must take under 5 ms on a low-end Android phone.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-c
tasks.notes: cross-section: Context (offline cache, 5 ms) and Decision (on-device evaluation, refresh interval); the superseded server-only passage is a trap.
